clue.text: Lad comes for punishment: he received suspended death sentence

indicators.note: the letters of 'Lad comes' are punished, knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A boy turns up to be disciplined, rather like a man once condemned to a hanging sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for punishment' is the anagram signal: LADCOMES is rearranged. The 'suspended death sentence' is a sword hung over his head by a single hair.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the courtier sat beneath a sword hanging by a hair, a threatened death held over him.

clue.text: Neat moves, to run browser

indicators.note: the letters of 'Neat' are moved about into a fresh order

parts.note: to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: A tidy move lets someone launch their internet browser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges NEAT into ANTE. 'browser' looks like computer software but is a grazing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A browser is an animal feeding on leaves and shoots, as many hoofed African grazers do.

clue.text: Bloody nonsense, my dear chap!

indicators.note: the letters of 'Bloody' are made nonsense of, jumbled into another order

explanation.surface: An exasperated Englishman dismisses something as rubbish while addressing a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody nonsense' reads as an oath, but 'nonsense' signals that BLOODY is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Old boy is a dated, chummy British form of address between men, like 'old chap'.

clue.text: Prepare a long time for such a holiday?

parts.note: to pack is to get one's luggage ready before travelling
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a trip takes ages, which suits a holiday booked all-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A package holiday bundles travel and accommodation together, sold as one deal.

clue.text: Try to identify candidate to take charge of school?

definitions.text: Try to identify candidate to take charge of school?

parts.words: Try to identify candidate to take charge of school?
parts.note: literally a hunt for a new head teacher, playfully describing the recruiting practice

explanation.surface: A school board searches for someone to lead the school.
explanation.definitionFit: Recruiters who poach executives are said to seek out talent this way, literally searching for a head.

clue.text: They go up the wall, as striptease performed

indicators.note: the letters of 'striptease' are performed in a different routine, rearranged

explanation.surface: Something sends people up the wall when a strip act is put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go up the wall' suggests being annoyed, but here it means being hung on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Woven wall hangings are literally hung up on walls as decoration.

clue.text: Hopefully, a spirited session

parts.note: a lively meeting, but 'spirited' means involving spirits of the dead, whom the sitters hope will appear

explanation.surface: Someone hopes a meeting will be lively.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting where people try to contact ghosts is, if it works, full of spirits.

clue.text: Moving along, aim for tree

indicators.note: the letters of 'along' and 'aim' are moving about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone moving along takes aim at a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a flowering tree or shrub with large showy blossoms.

clue.text: Very happy to be one of the family? Not at first

indicators.note: the word for a family member is used without its opening letter

parts.note: someone related is one of the family

explanation.surface: Someone is overjoyed to be accepted into a family, though not straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at first' takes the R off RELATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be elated is to be thrilled and in high spirits.

clue.text: See 2
Food for hotheads?

parts.note: 'bean' is slang for head, so beans that have been cooked are, jokingly, heads that are hot

explanation.surface: A question about what quick-tempered people eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bean' is old slang for the head, so cooked beans are 'hot heads'.
explanation.definitionFit: Haricots in tomato sauce, sold in tins, are an everyday British food.

clue.text: Brave, attempting the banjo?

definitions.meaning: a banjo is played by plucking strings, so one trying it is plucking

explanation.surface: Taking up the banjo needs courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluck means courage, so someone plucky is brave; jokingly, a banjo player is busy plucking.

clue.text: Exhausted, but well received as you leave

definitions.meaning: worn out, broken down from use
applauded as you go off stage

explanation.surface: A tired performer is cheered off at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn-out machinery is said to be finished in this slang way; literally, a departing performer is applauded off.

clue.text: One's on hand potentially to issue a challenge

definitions.text: One's on hand potentially to issue a challenge

parts.words: One's on hand potentially to issue a challenge
parts.note: a glove is worn on the hand, and throwing one down is the traditional way to challenge someone

explanation.surface: Someone is standing by, ready to issue a challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on hand' seems to mean available, but literally means worn on the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight threw down his armoured glove to challenge an opponent to combat.

clue.text: Attack a sailor verbally

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor

explanation.surface: Insulting a sailor amounts to an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbally' suggests abuse, but it signals that 'a salt' (sailor) is said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent attack on someone.

clue.text: Line, golden, from this poet?

parts.note: aureate means golden or gilded

explanation.surface: A poet produces a golden line of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A poet honoured with the official laurel is the nation's chosen versifier, the Poet in that title.

clue.text: Mean to keep recipe for such poor-quality meat

indicators.note: the word for mean holds the abbreviation within it

parts.note: stingy means mean, tight-fisted
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted cook keeps a recipe for cheap, tough meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough cheap meat full of fibres is described as being chewy and full of sinews.

clue.text: Not the chosen people — one is covered in maggots

indicators.note: the numeral for one is wrapped inside the word for maggots

parts.note: gentles are maggots, used by anglers as bait
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grim scene where someone is crawling with maggots.
explanation.walkthrough: GENTLES are maggots used as fishing bait in British angling.
explanation.definitionFit: Jews are traditionally called the chosen people; non-Jews are known by this term.

clue.text: Put off taking a day over most of magazine

indicators.note: in a down answer the first pieces are written over, above, the next
the word for magazine is used without its final letters

parts.note: a journal is a periodical or magazine

explanation.surface: Someone postpones reading, taking a day over most of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims JOURNAL to JOURN; 'over' places A and D above it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjourn a meeting is to postpone it to a later time.

clue.text: Enclosure is not simple

definitions.meaning: a fenced or walled area containing buildings

explanation.surface: Building a fenced area is not straightforward.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a walled yard and something composite, made of more than one element.

clue.text: From Reno, go travelling — north, to here

definitions.note: the destination lies to the north of the Nevada city

indicators.note: the letters of 'Reno' and 'go' travel into a new order

explanation.surface: Directions for a road trip heading north out of Reno.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges RENOGO; the state named borders Nevada to the north.
explanation.definitionFit: This US Pacific state lies directly north of Nevada, where the city of Reno is.

clue.text: Object to being given errand, not for the first time

parts.note: re- means again, so not for the first time
someone given an errand is sent on it

explanation.surface: Someone objects to being sent on an errand yet again.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter and aggrieved about it.

clue.text: Inclining to be collecting leaves

definitions.meaning: sloping, set at an angle, as a stage is
gathering fallen leaves with a garden tool

explanation.surface: Someone is tempted to spend the day gathering autumn leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A raked stage slopes; and a rake is the tined garden tool that gathers fallen leaves.

clue.text: Want extremely lucrative job: sewer business?

parts.note: to want is to need

indicators.note: only the extreme letters of 'lucrative' are taken

parts.note: work is a job

explanation.surface: Someone after a well-paid job ends up in the sewage trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' means a drain but here is one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing and embroidery are the trade of someone who stitches, so it is a stitcher's business.

clue.text: Careless mistakes with brickie's equipment

parts.note: slips are minor mistakes
a hod is the trough a bricklayer (brickie) carries bricks in

explanation.surface: A bricklayer makes errors with his tools.
explanation.walkthrough: A brickie is British slang for a bricklayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash, untidy work done without care is described with this word.

clue.text: See 24 across
Try sculpture and fail

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
a bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders

explanation.surface: An artist attempts a sculpture and it goes badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that collapses and goes bankrupt is said to fold in this way.

clue.text: In foreign currency, a few demanded money for freedom

indicators.note: the phrase for a few goes inside the currency name

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency
some means a few

explanation.surface: Kidnappers asked for a sum in foreign money to release a hostage.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnappers who held someone and asked payment for release did this to the captive.
